information: Kisan Call Centre (KCC) is a government telephone helpline launched by the Ministry of Agriculture on 21 January 2004 to use ICT in farming.
Toll-free number 1800-180-1551; works from mobile and landline on all telecom networks including private providers.
Calls answered 6.00 am to 10.00 pm, all seven days of the week, at each KCC location.
Replies are given in 22 local languages. The page does not list which 22; Hindi and Kannada coverage must be confirmed.

subtopic: Kisan Call Centre - how queries are answered
information: Farm Tele Advisors (agriculture graduates or allied-field degree holders) answer calls. Queries they cannot answer go to subject-matter specialists from State Agriculture Departments, ICAR and State Agricultural Universities via call conferencing. Operates from 14 locations covering all States and UTs.

Open dataset of district-wise, month-wise queries asked by farmers and answers given by FTAs. Fields listed: StateName, DistrictName, BlockName, Season, Sector. No record count or API on the listing page.

information: Rs 6,000 per year per family, paid in three equal instalments of Rs 2,000 every four months, via Direct Benefit Transfer.

Landholding farmer families with cultivable land in their own names (husband, wife and minor children count as one family). Urban land qualifies only if cultivated. Tenant farmers excluded. Land ownership cut-off date: 1 February 2019 (exception for land transferred by succession).

Excluded: institutional landholders; families of constitutional post holders, ministers, legislators, mayors or district panchayat chairpersons; serving or retired central/state government and PSU employees (Class IV/Group D staff not excluded); pensioners receiving Rs 10,000+ per month; anyone who paid income tax in the last assessment year; registered doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects.

eKYC is mandatory for registered farmers. OTP-based eKYC is on the PM-KISAN portal; biometric eKYC is at nearby CSC centres. Eligibility status (Know Your Status) is on the portal, the app, and the Kisan eMitra chatbot.
